title: From Exploration to Explanation: ML-Driven Causal Discovery for Datacenter Reliability at Scale
problem: Modern datacenters operate at massive scale with complex interdependencies across cooling, power, and network subsystems. Failures cascade through systems, and existing threshold or correlation-based monitoring cannot isolate root causes within high-dimensional, evolving telemetry.
motivation: Datacenters consume hundreds of megawatts and support critical HPC and AI workloads. Understanding causal pathways in system failures enables proactive reliability management and efficiency improvements.
method: PACE starts by grouping datacenter sensor readings into related patterns without needing labeled examples (unsupervised), then applies a time-aware causality detector called Granger causality to identify which measurements actually predict others—revealing genuine cause-and-effect relationships rather than just coincidental overlap. It produces visual maps (causal graphs and heatmaps) structured to match how the physical cooling, power, and network systems actually work and how their controls interact. These maps feed into digital twin models—computer replicas of the datacenter—enabling what-if analysis: predicting what happens if you adjust cooling by a certain amount or add more network capacity.
key_novelty: The core idea is pairing unsupervised pattern discovery with time-aware causal detection to automatically isolate root causes by tracing which sensor readings actually forecast others, rather than just detecting correlated symptoms.
contributions: PACE framework for datacenter causal discovery
Unsupervised correlation clustering for subsystem structure identification
Lag-aware Granger causality for directed causal pathways
Interpretable causal graphs and subsystem heatmaps
limitations: Specific evaluation metrics and case studies not detailed in abstract.
